fields.meta_description: Build a remote work survey from a prompt, with questions on home setup, office days, time zones, and team connection. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Remote Work Survey for Every Time Zone
fields.hero_description: Build a remote work survey that asks about home setup and meeting hours, and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Made for Teams That Rarely Share an Office
fields.features_subheading: A remote work survey asks people who work from home about their setup and their week. Emergent builds it from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Sections drafted from how the team works

Tell Emergent whether the team is fully remote or hybrid and what people should rate, like setup and meeting hours. It drafts a section per topic, and a prompt edits any question.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer in a database you own

Each answer is saved as a row, with the respondent's team and time zone beside it. The data lives in a database you own, and next year's results land in the same table.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Emergent can build the survey as a conversational flow that shows one question per screen. People can answer on a phone between calls instead of waiting for a free hour at a desk.
fields.feature_4:
Low scores sent to the person who acts

Set a rule, such as a team score under 3.0 on one question, and the app sends that team's results to a named person by Slack, email, or an in-app alert, with a reminder later.
fields.feature_5:
Names and teams from your HR tool

The app can connect to any HR tool with an API and pull each person's department and time zone. Answers arrive tagged, and nobody retypes the org chart into a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on GitHub

The survey can run on your own domain, which Emergent includes and which uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, ready to change or host.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Remote Surveys and Who Acts on Each
fields.tab_content_1:
11 missing monitors, one list for the IT lead

Okeford Labs asks its 64 remote staff what their home setup is missing. The survey is named, not anonymous, because IT has to ship each item to a person. The 11 who work without a second monitor land on one list for the IT lead, Imogen Rask, with each name and item.
fields.tab_content_2:
Tuesday is picked by 71 people for 40 desks

Cobbler Lane Studio's Denver office has 40 desks and is closed on Mondays. Its 112 people on a hybrid schedule pick the days they would come in. Tuesday drew 71 picks and Wednesday 64, while Friday drew 9. Office manager Teodor Blaine gets the counts by day and sets a team rotation for both busy days.
fields.tab_content_3:
Late calls fall on London: 5 of 6 engineers

Lumenhill Media's 18-person engineering team spans Pacific, Eastern, and London time. The survey asks how many calls a week start after 6 p.m. local time. In London, 5 of 6 engineers say 3 or more, against 1 of 7 on Pacific and 0 of 5 on Eastern. Their manager, Bram Stavely, sees the split by zone.
fields.tab_content_4:
Support scores 2.4 on help, and HR gets the results

Every quarter, Kestrelway Travel asks 4 team connection questions, rated 1 to 5. Any team averaging under 3.0 on knowing who to ask for help goes to the HR partner, Marisol Quade. This quarter, Support averaged 2.4 out of 5 from 26 answers, while Sales, Product, and Finance scored 3.6 or higher.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Remote Work Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a remote work survey that people in every time zone finish and that ends in a change they can see.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name what the answers could change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe the team in your prompt
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put one idea in each question
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask in each person's local time
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the decisions the results could feed before you draft a question, such as the equipment budget or the meeting schedule. Cut any question that feeds none of them. A survey built around 2 or 3 decisions stays short enough to finish.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent how many people will answer, whether they are fully remote or hybrid, and which time zones they work in. Emergent builds the survey and its response database from that prompt. Read the draft once as a respondent would.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pew Research Center's guidance says double-barreled questions are difficult for respondents to answer. Split any question that asks about two things. Ask about equipment in one question and internet speed in the next, each on the same 1 to 5 scale.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Phrase every time in the respondent's own zone: ask how many calls start after 6 p.m. your time, not after 3 p.m. Eastern. A London engineer and a Seattle engineer then answer the same question, and the split by zone holds up.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Keep it open for a full week
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open the survey on a Monday in the earliest time zone and close it the following Monday. That gives every zone 5 working days to answer. The app can send one reminder by email or Slack to the whole list on day 4.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the draft to 5 people before the full send, including someone in the latest time zone. Pew Research Center calls pretesting an essential step in questionnaire design. Ask each tester which question they read twice, and fix that one first.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within 2 weeks of the close, share the results with everyone who was asked. Name the 1 or 2 changes you will make and the answers behind them. Point back to those changes when the next round opens.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to ask in a remote working survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to ask in a remote working survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to ask in a remote working survey?

faq_plan.a: Good remote work survey questions cover home setup, schedule, meeting hours, team connection, and manager support. Ask whether people have the equipment they need, which days they would come in, how many calls start outside their working hours, and whether they know who to ask for help. Use one 1 to 5 scale for all of them.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a remote work survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder in plain English: who answers, which topics to cover, and what should happen when a team scores low. Emergent writes the questions and the table that stores the answers, and a follow-up prompt changes either one. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How do I adapt a remote work survey template for my team?
faq_plan.a: Start from a remote work survey template, then rewrite it for your team. Cut questions that will not change a decision, and add the details your team needs, like its time zones and office days. Emergent drafts the questions from a prompt that describes the team, and you edit them by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Should a remote work survey include questions about managers?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but keep it to 2 or 3, such as whether one-on-ones happen as planned and whether priorities are clear. For a full read on how one manager is doing, run a separate manager feedback survey and keep the remote work survey short.

faq_plan.q: Should a remote work survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Partly. Make the questions about team connection and managers anonymous, and run anything someone must act on, like an equipment request, as a separate named survey. In an anonymous survey, responses are completely separate from any personally identifiable information. In a confidential one, responses are connected to personal information.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a remote work survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it under 15 questions, with a single open question at the end. Group the rest into sections of 3 or 4 by topic. Putting the open question last means the scale questions get answered first.

faq_plan.q: Should new hires get the same remote work survey?
faq_plan.a: Not at first. Send people hired into remote roles an onboarding survey at 30 and 90 days instead. Ask whether their equipment arrived before day one, whether they have met their team, and who they go to with questions. After 90 days, add them to the regular remote work survey list.

faq_plan.q: How can a remote work survey compare remote and in-office employees?
faq_plan.a: Ask each person's work arrangement first: fully remote, hybrid, or in the office. Every later answer is saved next to that choice, and the results split by it. Keep the wording identical for all three groups. The app Emergent builds can also pull the arrangement from your HR system through its API instead of asking.

faq_plan.q: Should a remote work survey ask about productivity?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but ask what gets in the way of focused work instead of asking people to rate their own output. Questions like how many hours a week are free of meetings, or how often a slow reply holds up a task, point to something you can change.

faq_plan.q: How often should you run a remote work survey?
faq_plan.a: Run the full remote work survey once a year, and send a pulse survey of 4 or 5 questions each quarter in between. The quarterly round shows whether last year's changes held. Emergent puts no response caps on surveys, and each round can go to the whole company.

plan.angle: Searchers for a remote work survey want the questions to ask and a template to start from. Question lists and templates answer what to ask; this page shows four remote work surveys built from a prompt, each ending with one named person acting on the answers: missing monitors listed for the IT lead, weekday picks counted against 40 desks for the office manager, late calls broken down by time zone for an engineering manager, and a team scoring under 3.0 on connection sent to the HR partner. The FAQ covers what a builder asks next: which questions, templates, managers, anonymity, length, remote hires, comparing remote and office answers, acting on results, and how often to run it.
